provenance.citation: Lee S-H, Erber WN, Porwit A, Tomonaga M, Peterson LC, for the ICSH. ICSH guidelines for the standardization of bone marrow specimens and reports. Int J Lab Hematol 2008;30(5):349-364.
provenance.notes: M:E ratio composition follows ICSH 2008 §2.6. Categories are an aggregated subset of the ICSH nucleated differential count, not the full list.

description: Ten tallied categories, with band and segmented neutrophils counted separately — the distinction that 10-Type — Bands+Segs Combined merges. Choose it when your report requires a band percentage; note that REF-001 §3.9 records observer-dependent variability in that distinction ([S8]). No separate promyelocyte, plasma-cell or mast-cell rows — see category guidance for where those cells are recorded. Includes the blasts-of-non-erythroid-cells formula for comparison against pre-2016 reports (withdrawn by WHO 2016; see the calculation reference).

ME_ratio.label: M:E Ratio
ME_ratio.basis: ICSH 2008 §2.6: all granulocytes and monocytes and their precursors (myeloblasts, promyelocytes, myelocytes, metamyelocytes, band forms, segmented neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils, promonocytes, monocytes) over erythroblasts at all stages. Note that a competing convention excludes monocytes.

blasts_non_erythroid.label: Blasts (% non-erythroid)
blasts_non_erythroid.basis: Erythroleukaemia rule of the WHO 4th edition: blasts expressed as a percentage of non-erythroid cells. Withdrawn by the 2016 revision (Arber et al., Blood 2016;127:2391-2405) in favour of counting blasts against all nucleated cells; WHO 2022 and ICC 2022 retained that denominator. Retained here for comparison with historical reports; it is not the current diagnostic convention.

templates.outSentence: A {{total}}-cell count reveals {{blasts}}% blasts, {{myelo}}% myelocytes, {{meta}}% metamyelocytes, {{bands}}% bands, {{segs}}% segmented neutrophils, {{eos}}% eosinophils, {{baso}}% basophils, {{mono}}% monocytes, {{lymph}}% lymphocytes, and {{nrbc}}% erythroid precursors. M:E ratio {{ME_ratio}}.

thresholds.label: legacy non-erythroid blast threshold
thresholds.basis: Pre-2022 WHO rule, shown for comparison only.

specimenTypes.targetCountBasis: ICSH 2008 §2.6: at least 500 cells when a precise percentage of an abnormal cell type is required for diagnosis; at least 300 when the differential is not essential to it.

categoryNotes.lymph: Lymphocytes only. **Plasma cells have no category in this profile.** Do not count them here — record them in the morphology comment. Counting a plasma cell as a lymphocyte overstates the lymphoid percentage and depresses every other percentage, because the denominator grows. If plasma cells need quantifying, use the 14-Type Nucleated Differential, which has a plasma-cell category (ICSH 2008 §2.6 lists one).
categoryNotes.baso: Basophils only. **Mast cells have no category in this profile.** Do not count them here — record them in the morphology comment. ICSH 2008 §2.6 lists mast cells separately; the 14-Type Nucleated Differential provides that category.
categoryNotes.myelo: Myelocytes. **This profile has no separate promyelocyte category**; a marrow requiring the promyelocyte percentage should be counted in the 14-Type Nucleated Differential or the 10-Type Bands+Segs Combined profile, both of which have one.

templates.outSentence: A {{total}}-cell differential count of peripheral blood reveals: {{segs}}% segmented neutrophils, {{bands}}% band forms, {{lymph}}% lymphocytes, {{mono}}% monocytes, {{eos}}% eosinophils, {{baso}}% basophils, {{blasts}}% blasts, {{myelo}}% myelocytes, {{meta}}% metamyelocytes, and {{nrbc}}% nucleated RBCs.

specimenTypes.targetCountBasis: CLSI H20-A2 defines the reference method as two reviewers counting 200 cells each. 200 is one observer's share of it, which is what routine single-observer practice does — a documented default, not a claim to perform the reference method.
